newsitem.title: USA: Sen. Daschle opposes balanced budget amendment.
newsitem.headline: Sen. Daschle opposes balanced budget amendment.

text.p: Senate Democratic leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota said on Saturday that he opposed a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution that Republicans have given top priority and would likely pass.
Amid talks of the new bipartisan attitude in Washington, Republicans and Democrats remain divided over a balanced budget amendment and the breadth of any capital gains tax cut.

Daschle, appearing on CNN's "Evans and Novak" programme, said he opposed a broad-based capital gains tax cut, preferring a more targeted approach. Republicans, who have the majority in Congress, are pushing for a broad reduction in the capital gains tax.

"I think that everybody's got to make up their own mind," Daschle said on the balanced budget amendment. He said he would make a case to colleagues about "why we have to oppose the Republican proposal as it is right now."

The Democratic leader said he believed the Senate would in the end have the necessary votes to pass the amendment. "I think it's an uphill battle for us. I don't think that we're going to win," Daschle said.

The House will have a harder time mustering the votes to pass the amendment requiring a balanced budget. House Republicans set a Feb. 26 vote on the amendment, but acknowledged it would be a very close vote.
Daschle also said the Senate was likely to confirm Clinton nominees Anthony Lake to head the CIA and Alexis Herman as labour secretary.
